name: codeSplitter
line: Git for the agentic era: a code host where a dozen agents and people change the same files at once and nothing gets overwritten.

why.solves: Git was made for one person at one keyboard. Put a dozen coding agents on one repo and they overwrite each other, wait behind merges and leave you the conflicts.
why.need: You run more than one agent, or agents next to people, and want every change read by a person before it ships.
why.better: Other hosts merge by guessing from text. Here every line knows who wrote it, so three agents can change one file in the same moment. It is still real git (clone, pull and push work), agents get the same controls people do, and the free desktop app keeps your git going when a cloud is down.

name: eqosys
line: One account for every game and app here: sign in once and your friends, saves and games come with you.

why.solves: Every new game or app asks for one more account, and your friends and saves stay stuck inside each one.
why.need: You play more than one of these, or you are making a game and don't want to build sign-in, friends and cloud saves again.
why.better: A game with no server of its own can use it straight from its page. Each person's saves are sealed with their own key and kept in their own region. An agent can call the same tools a person clicks.

name: git-recon
line: A toy-soldier shooter fought in a codebase: the repo is the level, its files the buildings, up to 64 to a battle.

name: Two Fronts
line: Thunder Marines against the Wooka horde: a turn-based war, then three.js battles on six worlds and in orbit. AI, hotseat or a friend online.

name: Park Hide & Seek
line: 3D hide and seek in all 63 national parks, from Half Dome to Old Faithful; each player is sent only what they can see. Headed to the App Store first.

name: Skate Tech Park
line: A giant riderless fingerboard on park terrain: vert, grinds and rails, or the rocket roadster skin whose jets fire with every trick.

name: Alien Disc Golf
line: Nine holes between countries on a 3D globe, the disc carried by NOAA's real wind right now; loft it into the jet stream if you dare.

name: Druids Curse
line: The live multiplayer game Rusty Buns was first built for.

name: Super Spy Splat Shot
line: A spy game in the dark: scan a Gaussian-splat room, run the missions in your dossier and find 100 things in the fewest shots.

name: Excalibrawl
line: An hourly drawing fight between two models, refereed by a third.

name: Hippo Tycoon
line: Four greedy oil-baron hippos race to chomp the most oil from a jungle geyser; solo, couch, LAN or online, on whatever you have.

name: Mythic Masters
line: A 3D arena brawler of 76 folklore beasts where mass and height are real, from a 6 kg jackalope to a tonne of lake monster.

name: Delayed Reaction
line: A phone-first dub rhythm game: a ring calls a note down a neon tunnel and you answer it a bar later.

name: Splat Rooms
line: Hunt for objects in photo-real 3D rooms: the room blacks out, and every splat you fire lights the patch it lands on for good.

name: What Would Fantano Say?
line: Drop in a track, pick your best 15 seconds and get a parody review: a score, a verdict and the best and worst bits. Your phone does the listening.

name: Auto Rig
line: The IK engine: drop in a 3D model, get a skeleton, skin weights and inverse kinematics you can drag around, in Rust and TypeScript.

name: tscircuit Desktop
line: tscircuit's circuit editor as one desktop file, with a Rust engine up to 22x faster. It works; parked until tscircuit updates its own dependencies.

name: FM Groovebox
line: A twelve-track FM groovebox with a drum machine, step sequencer, piano roll and reverb.

name: GeoBoxQ
line: Will it fit in the box? Tell it your boxes and your products, and it names the smallest box that takes the whole order.

why.solves: Picking a shipping box by eye costs money on boxes that are too big, or ends with an order that doesn't fit.
why.need: You pack mixed orders and want the right box named before you start packing.
why.better: It knows a box can go in a box: a product that opens carries smaller ones inside it, level after level, which tools that treat every product as solid get wrong. No account, and your sizes stay in your browser.

name: Motion MIDI
line: One synth written twice, in Rust and in TypeScript, checked sample by sample: press play and race the two engines.

name: AT Lens
line: Type a handle and watch the AT Protocol work step by step, from domain to DID to data server, then follow the account live on the firehose.

name: ShareSplat
line: Photograph a product with your phone and shoppers can spin it round on your store page.

why.solves: A flat photo can't show a product from every side, and a 3D model used to need a studio or a 3D artist.
why.need: You sell online and want shoppers to turn the real product round before they buy.
why.better: A phone and a shot list that tells you each photo to take are enough. Your photos stay on your device until you choose to put a model online, and one pasted snippet (or the Shopify block) puts it on the page.

name: qCRM
line: The CRM your agents can use: customers, companies and deals for a small business, with every row yours to take away.

why.solves: Customer records end up locked in a CRM that an AI helper can only reach by clicking through screens, and that is hard to leave.
why.need: You want an agent to log the call, move the deal and tell you who to ring today, without you copying things by hand.
why.better: Agents are first-class: everything a person can do is a tool an agent can call, and the risky ones make it ask you first. The analysis runs in your own browser, and you can export or delete every row at any time.

name: Qollab
line: The multiplayer around your game, done: rooms, parties, friends online, chat and saves.

why.solves: Every multiplayer game ends up building the same lobby again: room codes, seats, ready flags, reconnects and chat.
why.need: You want friends playing your game together this week, not after a month of lobby work.
why.better: It leaves your game alone: your ticks, physics and data never pass through it. A party is one call, rooms are friends-only unless you say otherwise, mute, kick and report are built in, and a player's friends and party carry from one game to the next.

calls: One call from a signed-in page
note: Inside every game here: press With friends

name: Cron Swanson
line: Every scheduled job and reminder in one place: the nightly backups, the weekly check-ins, the yearly renewals.

why.solves: Scheduled jobs and reminders are spread over apps and dashboards, and nobody remembers why half of them exist.
why.need: You want one screen that shows every backup, check-in and renewal and when it last ran, and that pesters you about the ones a person has to do.
why.better: Each job carries why it exists and what it calls, not only a schedule. It fires on the minute, where the cloud alarms we tried came up to five minutes late, and it runs on any small computer you own.

name: hemyviz
line: Everything you have deployed, drawn live as a map, a city or a 3D scene: every stack, stage and resource.

why.solves: After a few deploys nobody can say what is running where: which stacks, which stages, which resources.
why.need: You deploy with Alchemy and want to see the whole fleet at once, and watch a deploy as it happens.
why.better: It needs no login and can't change a thing: it only reads the state files already on your disk. Leave it open during a deploy and watch each block go blue and settle green.

name: Splat Desktop
line: An open-source Gaussian-splat editor as a desktop app: open a folder of 3D scans of real places and edit them on your own disk.

name: Meshy Batch Studio
line: A folder of drawings in, game-ready 3D models out, through your own Meshy key, with nothing in between.

name: Agent Office
line: A cartoon 3D office where AI helpers sit at desks and write code, as one file for Mac and Linux.

name: Hello World
line: The smallest Rusty Buns app: one page, static assets only.

name: Sound Guy Simulator
line: A first-person sound-crew sim on real numbers: carry the gear at its real weight, roll out the cable, wire power and signal, and aim the speakers, from a garage to an arena.

name: QView3D
line: Shoppers put their own photo and words on a 3D hat, tee or hoodie, right on your shop's page.

why.solves: Shoppers can't see what their own photo or words will look like on a hat or a shirt before they buy, so they guess, or leave.
why.need: You sell custom-printed hats, tees or hoodies and want shoppers to design on the product itself.
why.better: It goes on the shop's own page with one script and one tag, takes the shop's colours, and loads only when a shopper scrolls to it. A pasted tag keeps working through our updates. A product we don't cover? Upload photos and get a model to print on.

name: One Team in 32
line: One page that shows how a single team's blitz rate drags a whole league's average, with a slider to try it.
